newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks firm in London ahead of CPI data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks firm in London ahead of CPI data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were mostly firmer in London in light trading on Tuesday as investors awaited the 1230 GMT release of the U.S. consumer price index (CPI), dealers said.
"The open on Wall Street will depend on these (CPI) numbers. People are just a bit cautious," said one dealer.
The consumer price index is expected to show a 0.2 percent rise in May after a 0.1 percent increase in April.
Figures on May housing starts also will be published at 1230 and data on May capacity utilisation and industrial production will be released at 1315 GMT.
Continued strength in the technology sector, which led Monday's late rebound in New York, underpinned market sentiment.

Shares in Motorola Inc were trading $1/8 higher to $68-7/8 in London after a report in the Wall Street Journal said the telecommunications giant planned to launch a $12.9 billion satellite network that would deliver high speed data and video.
"That's definitely of interest and we're waiting for analysts' comments on that," a dealer said.

After Wall Street closed on Monday, Micron Electronics Inc and Micron Technology Inc posted better-than-expected third quarter profits. Though the shares do not trade in London, dealers said the figures bolstered investor sentiment for the technology sector.
"All that should bode well for the market," the dealer added.
Among other high technology blue chips, shares in International Business Machines Corp firmed $1/4 to $89-5/8, while shares in Intel Corp rose $3/8 to $147-5/8.

In other trading, shares in General Motors Corp climbed $1/8 to 45-1/2 after the automaker and the United Auto Workers union reported progress on talks aimed at ending a strike at a Michigan truck plant.
Shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc were up $1/8 to $45-7/8 as investors awaited an industry wide settlement in tobacco negotiations. A deal was expected sometime this week, dealers said.
Elsewhere, September S&P 500 index futures were down 0.30 point to 903.85 on Globex, while September long bond futures were off 1/32 to 112-1/32.
